passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: We are a leading retailer and distributor of automotive replacement parts and accessories in the Americas. We began operations in 1979 and at August 29, 2026, operated 6,863 stores in the U.S., 1,001 stores in Mexico and 167 stores in Brazil. Each store carries an extensive product line for cars, sport utility vehicles, vans and light duty trucks, including new and remanufactured automotive hard parts, maintenance items, accessories and non-automotive products. At August 29, 2026, in 6,443 of our domestic stores as well as the vast majority of our stores in Mexico and Brazil, we had a commercial sales program that provides prompt delivery of parts and other products and commercial credit to local, regional and national repair garages, dealers, service stations, fleet owners and other accounts. We also sell automotive hard parts, maintenance items, accessories and non-automotive products through www.autozone.com, and our commercial customers can make purchases through www.autozonepro.com. Additionally, we sell the ALLDATA brand of automotive diagnostic, repair, collision and shop management software through www.alldata.com. We also provide product information on our Duralast branded products through www.duralastparts.com. We do not derive revenue from automotive repair or installation services. Executive Summary For fiscal 2026, net sales increased to $20.3 billion, a 7.4% increase over the prior year. Domestic commercial sales increased 10.6%, which represents 33.1% of our total Domestic sales . Operating profit increased 3.1% to $3.7 billion, net income increased 3.0% to $2.6 billion and diluted earnings per share increased 5.3% to $152.55 for the year. Fiscal 2026 comparisons were positively impacted by foreign currency exchange rates which had a favorable impact to net sales of $254.4 million and operating profit of $73.9 million, and IEEPA tariff refunds which has a positive impact on operating profit of $96.0 million. Operating profit comparison was also negatively impacted by an unfavorable net non-cash LIFO impact of $128.0 million. During fiscal 2026, failure and maintenance related categories represented the largest portion of our sales mix, at approximately 85% of total sales. We have not experienced any fundamental shifts in our category sales mix as compared to previous years. Our business is impacted by various factors within the economy that affect both our consumer and our industry, including but not limited to inflation, interest rates, levels of consumer debt, fuel and energy costs, prevailing wage rates, foreign exchange rate fluctuations, supply chain disruptions, tariffs, trade policies and other geopolitical factors, hiring and other economic conditions. Given the nature of these macroeconomic factors, which are generally outside of our control, we cannot predict whether or for how long certain trends will continue, nor can we predict to what degree these trends will impact us in the future. ​ The two statistics we believe have the closest correlation to our market growth over the long-term are miles driven and the number of seven-year-old or older vehicles on the road. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Our business is subject to a variety of risks and uncertainties. The risk factors described below reflect the Company's beliefs and opinions as to factors that could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, liquidity and stock price or otherwise impact the Company. References to past events are provided by way of example only and are not intended to be a complete listing or a representation as to whether such factors have occurred in the past or their likelihood of occurring in the future. The following information should be read in conjunction with the other information contained in this report and other filings that we make with the SEC. These risks and uncertainties are not the only ones we face. Our business could also be materially affected by additional factors that are presently unknown to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial to our business. Strategic and Operational Risks ​ The current global economic and geopolitical landscape has increased uncertainty about key areas of doing business internationally and may have a negative impact on our business. ​ The U.S. has recently enacted and proposed to enact significant new tariffs, and the current administration has directed various federal agencies to further evaluate key aspects of U.S. trade policy amid ongoing discussion regarding further potentially significant changes to U.S. trade policies, enforcement priorities, sanctions, treaties and tariffs. In February 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court invalidated tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (“IEEPA”). In response to the U.S. Supreme Court’s decision, the U.S. President issued an executive order imposing tariffs pursuant to Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 for 150 days, effective on February 24, 2026, and the outlook on further trade policy actions is unclear. These actions have led to significant volatility and uncertainty in global markets. Uncertainty regarding the scope, duration and administration of trade measures has in the past contributed to, and may in the future continue to contribute to, variability in costs and cash flows. There continues to exist significant uncertainty about the future economic and political relationships between the U.S. and other countries. The Company directly or indirectly imports merchandise from various countries, and newly proposed tariffs and any additional tariffs on products sourced from these or other countries could materially increase our costs. credit_strengths.text: Operating margin sits well above the consumer discretionary sector median, reflecting AutoZone's commercial program penetration and failure-and-maintenance sales mix, which is less discretionary than general retail. This pricing and mix advantage underpins stable operating income through the cycle.

Operating cash flow comfortably covers the disclosed buyback outlay, and cash generation has risen each year across the disclosed trend. Internal funding therefore supports both capital spending and the bulk of shareholder returns without incremental borrowing.

key_risks.text: Gross leverage sits modestly above the sector median and net leverage is a multiple of the sector median, so the balance sheet carries more debt than peers. Headroom to the next risk-band boundary is negligible, leaving little cushion against an EBITDA setback.

The risk factors flag tariff and trade-policy volatility, including measures imposed after the Supreme Court invalidated prior IEEPA tariffs, as a source of cost and cash-flow variability. AutoZone imports merchandise directly and indirectly, so duty changes could compress margins and working capital.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is solid and improved year over year, sitting in line with the sector median. Operating income covers gross interest expense several times over, so earnings comfortably absorb the current coupon burden even with commercial paper priced near the prior year's level.

Free cash flow to debt is below the sector median and slipped year over year, while the current ratio is below one and below peers. Near-term maturities plus commercial paper reliance mean refinancing access, not balance-sheet liquidity, carries the repayment burden.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is intermediate, with leverage just inside the first band and cash-flow coverage in the second tier. Deleveraging has been marginal year over year, and the upgrade path requires either meaningful EBITDA growth or debt reduction that current distribution policy does not obviously support.

The debt stack is laddered senior notes with commercial paper layered on top and a revolving facility maturing later, so refinancing is staggered rather than clustered. Our judgement is that access to the commercial paper and revolver markets, rather than retained cash, is the swing factor for near-term maturities.

credit_strengths.text: 營業利潤率遠高於非必需消費品行業中位數，反映AutoZone商業計劃的滲透率以及故障與維護銷售組合，該組合較一般零售更具非必需消費品性質。此定價與組合優勢支撐整個週期內穩定的營業收入。
經營現金流足以輕鬆覆蓋所披露的回購支出，且現金產生在所披露趨勢中逐年上升。因此，內部資金可同時支持資本支出及大部分股東回報，而無需增量借款。

key_risks.text: 總槓桿略高於行業中位數，淨槓桿為行業中位數的倍數，因此資產負債表所承載的債務多於同業。距下一風險區間邊界的餘裕微乎其微，對EBITDA挫折的緩衝甚少。
風險因素標示關稅及貿易政策波動，包括最高法院裁定先前IEEPA關稅無效後所實施的措施，為成本及現金流變動的來源。AutoZone直接及間接進口商品，因此關稅變動可能壓縮利潤率及營運資金。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率穩健且同比改善，與行業中位數一致。營業收入覆蓋總利息支出數倍，因此即使商業票據定價接近上年水平，盈利仍能輕鬆吸收當前票息負擔。
自由現金流對債務比率低於行業中位數且同比下滑，而流動比率低於一且低於同業。近期到期債務加上對商業票據的依賴，意味著償還負擔在於再融資渠道而非資產負債表流動性。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為中等，槓桿恰在第一區間之內，現金流覆蓋處於第二檔。去槓桿同比幅度輕微，升級路徑需要顯著的EBITDA增長或債務削減，而當前分配政策並未明顯支持後者。
債務結構為階梯式高級票據，上層疊加商業票據，以及較後到期的循環融資，因此再融資為錯開而非集中。我們的判斷是，對於近期到期債務，商業票據及循環貸款市場的准入而非留存現金，才是關鍵變數。
